question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides protection to persons arrested or detained under the preventive detention law?
solution:
​The correct answer is __**Article 22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 22** of the Indian Constitution guarantees certain procedural safeguards to individuals in the** case of arrest and detention** in certain cases.
 
• This article applies to both** citizens and non-citizens**.
 
• This provision extends some procedural safeguards to individuals in the case of arrest.
 
• It comes into play after a person has been arrested. **It is not a fundamental right against arrest and detention**.
 
• The idea behind this right is to prevent arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
• This provision provides the following safeguards:
 
 
• **Article 22(1)** - Any person who is in custody must be informed of the grounds for his or her arrest. Additionally, he or she cannot be denied the right to consult with a lawyer.
 
• **Article 22(2)** - The arrested person must be produced before a judicial magistrate within 24 hours of his or her arrest.
 
• **Article 22(3)** - No person arrested under a preventive detention law can be detained for a period longer than the period specified by the judicial magistrate.
 
 
 
• **However, these safeguards do not apply to**:
 
 
• Enemy aliens
 
• Foreigners
 
• Persons arrested under preventive detention laws
 
 

Article 22 of the Indian Constitution **ensures the right not to be subjected to abuse during arrest **or while in custody. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are two types of detention:
 
 
• Penal detention is detention after trial.
 
• Preventive detention is detention without trial.
 
• The idea behind this is to prevent a person from committing a crime. This means that individuals can be detained on suspicion.
 
• The rights of persons arrested in this manner are governed by preventive detention laws.
